title: Connect buttons, events, and state
outcome: Add a real message through a form and update the visible inbox.
story: Amina’s page has fields and buttons, but they do not do anything yet. Connect the form to a list of messages and show what actually happened.

demo.title: Connect an action to a result

frames.explanation: An event updates the data, then rendering updates the screen.
An error explains the problem without adding an empty record.

sections.title: The DOM is the page as objects
paragraphs: The browser turns HTML into a document object model, or DOM. JavaScript can find an element with document.getElementById and change its textContent. This connects the data in a program to the visible page.

Use textContent when displaying a customer’s message. It treats the content as text. Setting innerHTML with untrusted text can create elements or scripts the person never intended to author for your page.

sections.title: An event tells you something happened
paragraphs: Submitting a form or pressing a button creates an event. addEventListener connects an event type to a function. The function can read fields, validate input, change state, and show a result.

Call event.preventDefault() when your JavaScript handles the form locally. Otherwise the browser’s default submission can navigate away from the page. Keep the native form and button so keyboard users can trigger the same behaviour.

sections.title: Keep state and rendering separate
paragraphs: State is the data the application is keeping track of now. Our messages array is state. A render function reads that array and draws the count and list. It does not invent a second, conflicting source of truth.

After adding a record to messages, call render again. Clear the list before recreating its items so old records do not appear twice. A stable identifier will help when later features answer or remove a particular message.

sections.title: Handle a failed action clearly
paragraphs: Trim whitespace before deciding whether a message is empty. If it is empty, show Write a message first and leave the state unchanged. If it is valid, add it, clear the field, and show Added.

Test the sequence a person actually uses, including keyboard submission and a second message. Also try text that looks like HTML. It should appear as text in the list, without being interpreted as a new element.

words.meaning: The browser’s object representation of the page.
A notification that an interaction or another action happened.
The data an application is keeping track of now.

example.code:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1"><title>Amina's shop</title><style></style></head><body><button id="add">Add 1 message</button><output id="count">10</output><script>let messages=10; document.getElementById("add").addEventListener("click",()=>{messages+=1;document.getElementById("count").textContent=messages;});</script></body></html>
example.output: Pressing Add 1 message changes the count from 10 to 11.
explanation: The program starts with state equal to 10.
The listener responds when the button is activated.
It changes the state and updates the output element.

cases.label: The initial count matches the state
cases.why: The screen should be a view of the actual state.

cases.label: The initial message is visible
cases.why: Rendering must show the data, not only a number.

cases.label: A submitted message updates the inbox without navigation
cases.script: document.getElementById("body").value="My order is late"; const event=new Event("submit",{bubbles:true,cancelable:true}); document.getElementById("form").dispatchEvent(event); return event.defaultPrevented && document.getElementById("count").textContent==="2" && document.getElementById("list").textContent.includes("My order is late");
cases.why: The event must update state and the screen while preserving the page.

cases.label: Blank input leaves the state unchanged
cases.script: const before=document.getElementById("count").textContent; document.getElementById("body").value="   "; document.getElementById("form").dispatchEvent(new Event("submit",{bubbles:true,cancelable:true})); return document.getElementById("count").textContent===before && document.getElementById("status").textContent==="Write a message first";
cases.why: A rejected action should explain the problem without changing the data.

cases.label: HTML-looking customer text remains text
cases.script: document.getElementById("body").value=""; document.getElementById("form").dispatchEvent(new Event("submit",{bubbles:true,cancelable:true})); return !document.querySelector("#list img") && document.getElementById("list").textContent.includes("");
cases.why: Customer content must not become executable page markup.
